gobel_city.title: Heinrich Göbel | Stadt Springe

observations.locator: Extracted text lines 184-184; locate by quoted text
observations.excerpt: Die Springer Bürger ehrten seit 1929 Heinrich Göbel als Erfinder der Glühlampe, was an verschiedenen Stellen in der Stadt sichtbar ist. Das Göbelhaus in seiner schlichten Ausstrahlung lässt nicht vermuten, dass hier in der Straße Zum Oberntor 30 einst Heinrich Göbel lebte. Ein Bronzerelief mit einer ewig brennenden Glühlampe erinnert an den 1848 nach New York emigrierten Springer Bürger. Im Museum auf dem Burghof befasst sich eine Abteilung mit Heinrich Göbel. So kann man dort erfahren, dass man glaubte, Heinrich Göbel habe kurz vor seinem Tode in einem Prozess die gebührende Anerkennung erhalten, bereits 25 Jahre vor dem Amerikaner Thomas Edison eine gebrauchsfertige Glühlampe erfunden zu haben. Diese Geschichte wird hier aber auch aus der Sicht Hans-Christian Rohdes beleuchtet, der in seiner Dissertation von 2007 die Erfindung der Glühlampe durch Heinrich Göbel zu widerlegen versucht.

gobel_city.actual_support_and_limitations: Explicit 1848 emigration to New York supports settlement; invention-priority legends on the page are disputed and are not evidence for this residence judgment.

bengio_cifar.title: Yoshua Bengio – CIFAR

observations.locator: Extracted text lines 57-61; locate by quoted text
observations.excerpt: Renewed Canada CIFAR AI Chair – 2023 Recognized worldwide as one of the leading experts in artificial intelligence, Yoshua Bengio is most known for his pioneering work in deep learning, earning him the 2018 A.M. Turing Award, “the Nobel Prize of Computing,” with Geoffrey Hinton and Yann LeCun. He is a Full Professor at Université de Montréal, and the Founder and Scientific Director of Mila – Quebec AI Institute. He co-directs the CIFAR Learning in Machines & Brains program as Senior Fellow and acts as Scientific Director of IVADO. In 2019, he was awarded the prestigious Killam Prize and in 2021, became the second most cited computer scientist in the world. He is a Fellow of both the Royal Society of London and Canada and Officer of the Order of Canada. Concerned about the social impact of AI and the objective that AI benefits all, he actively contributed to the Montreal Declaration for the Responsible Development of Artificial Intelligence.

bengio_cifar.actual_support_and_limitations: Documents Canadian appointments/current achievements, not the earlier US posting or its residential nature. Omission is not false evidence.
